title: Hanuman Took the Mountain Back
source: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 6.61 (Critical Edition; vulgate 6.74)

captions.instagram:
Most of us know one herb-mountain trip: for Lakshmana. But in Valmiki's Ramayana, Hanuman makes an earlier one. Indrajit's Brahmastra had felled BOTH Rama and Lakshmana and much of the army. At night, old Jambavan, blinded by arrows, asks first: "Is Hanuman alive?" because while Hanuman lives, the army is not beaten. On the Himalaya the herbs hide from Hanuman, so he lifts the whole peak and flies on the sun's path like a second sun. The fragrance alone heals everyone, and then he carries the mountain back to the Himalaya. Part 2: the trip we all know.

Did you know Hanuman returned the mountain the first time? 👇 Part 2 tomorrow. Jai Bajrang Bali!

📜 Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 6.61 (Critical Edition; vulgate 6.74)

captions.youtube_description:
Most of us know one herb-mountain trip: for Lakshmana. But in Valmiki's Ramayana, Hanuman makes an earlier one. Indrajit's Brahmastra had felled BOTH Rama and Lakshmana and much of the army. At night, old Jambavan, blinded by arrows, asks first: "Is Hanuman alive?" because while Hanuman lives, the army is not beaten. On the Himalaya the herbs hide from Hanuman, so he lifts the whole peak and flies on the sun's path like a second sun. The fragrance alone heals everyone, and then he carries the mountain back to the Himalaya. Part 2: the trip we all know.

Did you know Hanuman returned the mountain the first time? 👇 Part 2 tomorrow. Jai Bajrang Bali!

Source: Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda 6.61 (Critical Edition; vulgate 6.74)
Verses:
• Indrajit's Brahmastra struck down Rama and Lakshmana — 6.61.1-4
• Sixty-seven crore monkeys were struck down — 6.61.12
• At night Hanuman and Vibhishana searched the field with torches — 6.61.7
• Jambavan, aged and covered with arrows, could not see and knew Vibhishana by his voice — 6.61.14-17
• Jambavan asked whether Hanuman still lived — 6.61.18
• Vibhishana asked why he asked of Hanuman and not the princes — 6.61.19-20
• While Hanuman lives the beaten army is unbeaten; if he dies we are dead though alive — 6.61.22
• Hanuman clasped Jambavan's feet — 6.61.24
• Jambavan sent him to the Himalaya, to the herb mountain between Rishabha and Kailasa, with four herbs — 6.61.29-34
• The herbs, knowing a seeker was coming, hid — 6.61.58
• Hanuman reproached the mountain for showing no compassion to Raghava and threatened it with the might of his arms — 6.61.59-60
• He uprooted the whole peak — 6.61.61
• On the sun's path he shone like a rival sun — 6.61.63
• The herbs' fragrance alone freed both princes of their arrows; the monkey heroes rose — 6.61.67
• He carried the herb mountain back to the Himalaya and rejoined Rama — 6.61.68
• There is a second herb-mountain trip later, for Lakshmana — 6.89.13-21

verify_note: CE 6.61.1-4,12: Indrajit's Brahmastra fells Rama, Lakshmana and 67 crore monkeys. 6.61.7,13-17: Hanuman and Vibhishana search with torches at night; old Jambavan, covered in arrows, can't see, knows Vibhishana by voice. 6.61.18: asks if Hanuman lives. 6.61.19-20: Vibhishana asks why Hanuman before the princes. 6.61.21-22: 'while he lives the beaten army is unbeaten; if he dies we are dead though alive'. 6.61.24: Hanuman clasps his feet. 6.61.29-34: Himalaya, between Rishabha and Kailasa, four herbs. 6.61.58: the herbs hide. 6.61.59-61: angry speech to the mountain, uproots the peak. 6.61.63: like a rival sun on the sun's path. 6.61.67: the fragrance frees both princes of arrows; monkey heroes rise. 6.61.68: he carries the mountain back to the Himalaya and rejoins Rama. 6.88.30-35: Ravana hurls the Maya-made shakti; it strikes Lakshmana's chest. 6.89.9-16: Sushena: not dead; sends Hanuman to the mountain 'described before by Jambavan'. 6.89.17-21: he doesn't know the herbs, brings the peak. 6.89.22-24: Sushena crushes the herb, gives it through the nose; Lakshmana rises. Hanuman Chalisa ch. 11 (ramcharit.in). Ramcharitmanas Lanka Kand: Meghnad's shakti (before doha 54), 'देखा सैल न औषध चीन्हा। सहसा कपि उपारि गिरि लीन्हा॥' (after doha 56).
